items.label: f01-three-successes
items.front: Name the three layers a Shopify GraphQL mutation must pass before the client records success.
items.back: Transport (an HTTP 200 response), the GraphQL envelope (no top-level errors), and the mutation payload (no userErrors and a created resource ID present).

items.label: f03-hash-not-auth
items.front: What does the plan's hash prove, and what does it not?
items.back: It detects changed normalized content. It is not authorization or a signature, and the preflight is a snapshot: another writer can still change the target after export and before a create.

items.label: f02-timeout-uncertainty
items.front: Why does a mutation timeout stop the migration instead of retrying, while some reads are retried?
items.back: The remote may have committed without returning an ID, so a retry could duplicate or collide on the handle; reads are retried only for selected statuses or throttling, and a fresh export is required after a mutation failure.

items.prompt: A fresh, unedited plan has 3 creates and 1 conflict. What does applyPlan send to the target store?

choices.text: The creates that come before the conflict in the plan
Nothing - any conflict aborts with 'Plan has conflicts; no mutation was sent.'
The 3 creates; the conflict is skipped and reported
All 3 creates plus a placeholder for the conflicting item

choices: The creates that come before the conflict in the plan
Nothing - any conflict aborts with 'Plan has conflicts; no mutation was sent.'
The 3 creates; the conflict is skipped and reported
All 3 creates plus a placeholder for the conflicting item

items.explanation: The conflict check runs after the staleness check and before the first journal write or mutation.

items.prompt: Someone hand-edits a reviewed plan.json to add an extra createEntry, leaving sourceHash and targetHash untouched, then runs apply. What happens?

choices.text: Apply refuses: it re-exports both stores, rebuilds the plan and finds the canonical forms differ ('Plan is stale or changed')
Apply skips the hash check when the operation count grows
Apply runs the extra create, because both hashes still match
Apply runs only the operations whose hashes it can verify

choices: Apply refuses: it re-exports both stores, rebuilds the plan and finds the canonical forms differ ('Plan is stale or changed')
Apply skips the hash check when the operation count grows
Apply runs the extra create, because both hashes still match
Apply runs only the operations whose hashes it can verify

items.explanation: The hashes are change detectors, not signatures. Apply compares the whole supplied plan against a freshly rebuilt one, so the plan file cannot become an arbitrary-mutation script.

items.prompt: The target has an entry whose handle does not appear in the source export. What does the plan do with it?

choices.text: Records it as a conflict that blocks apply
Copies it back into the source snapshot
Plans a delete so the target mirrors the source
Lists it in targetOnly and leaves it alone - absence from a source export is not evidence for deletion

choices: Records it as a conflict that blocks apply
Copies it back into the source snapshot
Plans a delete so the target mirrors the source
Lists it in targetOnly and leaves it alone - absence from a source export is not evidence for deletion

items.explanation: The planner has no delete operation at all; target-only entries are reported for review and retained.

items.prompt: A definition marks title as required, and a source entry has title set to the empty string. What happens when the snapshot is normalized?

choices.text: It passes, because the field key is present
It passes, and the target store rejects it later at create time
The entry is skipped and reported in targetOnly
It throws 'Required entry field is missing.' - an empty string counts as missing, just like null

choices: It passes, because the field key is present
It passes, and the target store rejects it later at create time
The entry is skipped and reported in targetOnly
It throws 'Required entry field is missing.' - an empty string counts as missing, just like null

items.explanation: A required field must have some value that is neither null nor ''. Validation happens in normalizeSnapshot, before any plan is written.

items.prompt: Apply has created operations 0 and 1; operation 2 fails. What state is left behind?

choices.text: Apply retries operation 2 automatically until it succeeds
Creates 0 and 1 stay in the target; the receipt is marked stopped with failed index 2, and the error says to re-export before retrying
Creates 0 and 1 are rolled back, leaving the target untouched
Apply skips operation 2 and continues with the rest

choices: Apply retries operation 2 automatically until it succeeds
Creates 0 and 1 stay in the target; the receipt is marked stopped with failed index 2, and the error says to re-export before retrying
Creates 0 and 1 are rolled back, leaving the target untouched
Apply skips operation 2 and continues with the rest

items.explanation: There is no rollback: the journal is a recovery aid that records confirmed creates. The thrown error carries the in-memory result even if the final journal write fails.

items.prompt: What does buildPlan do when the source and target snapshots name the same store?

choices.text: It returns an empty plan with every entry unchanged
It plans creates for every entry, duplicating them
It throws 'Source and target stores must differ.' before planning anything
It warns and continues

choices: It returns an empty plan with every entry unchanged
It plans creates for every entry, duplicating them
It throws 'Source and target stores must differ.' before planning anything
It warns and continues

items.explanation: Migrating a store onto itself is refused outright; applyPlan re-checks the same invariant on the clients.

items.prompt: Under canonical(), do { b: 1, a: 2 } and { a: 2, b: 1 } produce the same string? Do [1, 2] and [2, 1]?

choices.text: The objects do - stable() sorts object keys recursively - but the arrays do not, because array order is preserved
The arrays match but the objects do not
Both pairs match, because stable() sorts arrays too
Neither pair matches, because JSON.stringify keeps insertion order

choices: The objects do - stable() sorts object keys recursively - but the arrays do not, because array order is preserved
The arrays match but the objects do not
Both pairs match, because stable() sorts arrays too
Neither pair matches, because JSON.stringify keeps insertion order

items.explanation: stable maps arrays element-wise without sorting and rebuilds objects from Object.keys(value).sort(). Order-insensitive collections are sorted explicitly in normalizeSnapshot instead (by key, handle, type).

items.prompt: Planning the example fixtures against an empty target yields one createDefinition and one createEntry. Why must they appear in that order?

choices.text: Order does not matter; applyPlan runs operations in parallel
The entry's type does not exist in the target until its definition is created - and applyPlan executes operations strictly in array order
Entries are created first so the definition can validate them
They are sorted alphabetically by kind, which happens to put definitions first

choices: Order does not matter; applyPlan runs operations in parallel
The entry's type does not exist in the target until its definition is created - and applyPlan executes operations strictly in array order
Entries are created first so the definition can validate them
They are sorted alphabetically by kind, which happens to put definitions first

items.explanation: buildPlan pushes createDefinition before looping over that definition's entries, and applyPlan iterates current.operations by index.

items.prompt: The target already has an entry with the same handle as a source entry, but one field value differs. What does buildPlan do with it?

choices.text: Marks it unchanged, because handles are the entry identity
Plans an update that overwrites the target value with the source value
Plans a create with a suffixed handle such as handle-2
Records a conflict ('Existing entry differs; update policy must be reviewed.') - the planner never updates existing entries

choices: Marks it unchanged, because handles are the entry identity
Plans an update that overwrites the target value with the source value
Plans a create with a suffixed handle such as handle-2
Records a conflict ('Existing entry differs; update policy must be reviewed.') - the planner never updates existing entries

items.explanation: A matching handle is compared canonically: equal goes to unchanged, different goes to conflicts. The utility only creates missing content.

items.prompt: A source entry has an optional field whose value is null. How does that field appear in the planned createEntry input?

choices.text: The whole entry is rejected as incomplete
It is converted to an empty string, since create input accepts text only
It is sent with an explicit null so the target clears that field
It is omitted - fields with null values are filtered out of the create input

choices: The whole entry is rejected as incomplete
It is converted to an empty string, since create input accepts text only
It is sent with an explicit null so the target clears that field
It is omitted - fields with null values are filtered out of the create input

items.explanation: The input is built with entry.fields.filter((f) => f.value !== null).map(({ key, value })); the field type is dropped too, since create input takes key/value only.

items.prompt: A source definition has one product_reference field among several text fields. How does buildPlan treat that definition?

choices.text: It creates the definition and sets every reference value to null
It creates the definition without the reference field
The whole definition becomes a conflict - reference fields need cross-store ID mapping, and none are silently dropped
It creates the definition and copies the source product IDs as-is

choices: It creates the definition and sets every reference value to null
It creates the definition without the reference field
The whole definition becomes a conflict - reference fields need cross-store ID mapping, and none are silently dropped
It creates the definition and copies the source product IDs as-is

items.explanation: Any field whose type includes 'reference' blocks the definition with an explicit reason; a source-store product ID is meaningless in the target store.
